newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris up on CREF news.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris up on CREF news.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc shares rallied 1-3/4 to 99-5/8 after College Retirement Equities Fund participants rejected a resolution urging divestment of the fund's tobacco-related holdings, analysts said.
They said the overall environment for tobacco stocks was better than it was a month ago and, with the U.S. election over, attacks on the industry may subside.
"I think its has to do with the CREF saying it will not divest itself of its tobacco holdings," said Ron Morrow, who covers the tobacco industry for Rodman & Renshaw Capital Group.

"Now that the election is over, you may see a little less aggressive anti-tobacco rhetoric and a higher likelihood of a compromise between the Clinton Administration and the tobacco industry," Morrow said.
Martin Feldman, tobacco analyst at Smith Barney said he expected the tobacco stocks to outperform the rest of the market for the next few months.
"The market is still digesting the fact that there are no major individual cases in 1996 and early 1997 and the outlook for policy in Congress has imrpoved since the election," he said.

He said that he expected Philip Morris' earnings per share to grow 18 percent in 1996 and 17 percent in 1997 compared with a Smith Barney forecast of three percent growth in overall Standard & Poor's 500 earnings next year.
